feedback: The RM correctly encodes the mutual-exclusion task (key vs. ball) with violation sinks and rewards are sparse/bounded, and per-state else self-loops cover irrelevant events. However, several issues: (1) In state u_ball, the transition (u_ball, door_open & has_door_key) -> u_ready is dead code: entering u_ball from u0 requires !has_door_key, and (u_ball, has_door_key) -> u_violation fires first on any step where has_door_key is true, so the second transition can never trigger; a door_open transition from u_ball without has_door_key is also impossible (door_open cannot precede has_door_key), leaving no legitimate path from u_ball to completion — the agent that moves the ball first is forever trapped in violation on picking up the key, even though door_open could in principle be reached via that path only with a violation anyway (this is consistent with the task). (2) State u_key has no transition for door_open & blocker_moved being needed? Actually blocker_moved from u_key fires the violation first, which is the intended constraint, so that is fine. (3) u_violation is declared in FINAL_STATES but is a rejecting/violation sink; this may be acceptable but should be noted — a violation state is absorbing with no terminal reward, which is fine for safety tasks. (4) More critically: the transition (u_key, blocker_moved) -> u_violation fires when blocker_moved becomes true while in u_key, but the agent could legitimately carry the key while the ball is already moved — no, wait: if the agent had moved the ball first it would be in u_ball, so u_key with blocker_moved implies key taken first then ball moved, a genuine violation. Consistent. (5) The violation is not quite right for the ordering: u0 -> u_key requires has_door_key & !blocker_moved, but if both become true in the same step the (u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key) violation catches it — good. (6) Missing: transition from u_key on !door_open losing key? Dropping the key in u_key keeps state u_key via else, fine. (7) The real defect: from u_ball there is no path to u_done at all, since has_door_key from u_ball always leads to violation — this makes the RM reject all valid solutions that move the ball first, but the task explicitly forbids ever having both, and since door_open requires has_door_key, moving the ball first can never lead to opening the door without violation. So u_ball is a de facto dead state; the reward (u_ball, door_open & has_door_key, u_ready) is unreachable dead transition/reward — violates compactness/ordered-transition-coverage. Remove it and the u_ball state, or restructure so that u_ball allows acquiring the key only if the ball remains moved... but that would be the violation per the task ('never both'), so u_ball should simply be a sink or removed. (8) Also, no reward on u0->u_key etc. is fine, but there is no guidance/dense reward shaping; acceptable for safety-style tasks. Fix: remove the unreachable (u_ball, door_open & has_door_key) transition and reward, and simplify u_ball accordingly.
